key_insight: The paper argues that long-horizon LLM agents fail when recursive memory summaries become ambiguous, and proposes optimizing memory quality by minimizing the uncertainty those summaries induce about the latent task state.
engineering_relevance: For building reliable agents, this suggests memory policies should be trained with fine-grained uncertainty-aware feedback, not just sparse task success signals.
method: Define Belief Entropy as a self-supervised proxy for uncertainty about the latent task state given current memory.
Use Metacognitive Memory Policy Optimization (MMPO) to penalize summaries that create high epistemic uncertainty.
Provide memory-specific supervision to reduce semantic noise and belief deviation during recursive summarization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that MMPO outperforms prior methods on diverse long-horizon tasks and retains 97.1% performance even at 1.75M-token context length.
watch_item: Belief-entropy estimates may be sensitive to proxy quality and implementation details, so the method’s robustness depends on how well uncertainty is calibrated.
paper_title: Meta-Cognitive Memory Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
